mainEntity.name: How do I know if my existing home structure can handle a second-story addition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You need a structural assessment by an engineer or qualified design-build contractor to determine if your foundation and framing can support a second story. Visual inspection alone isn’t enough because the loads and code requirements are significant.

Sometimes an existing foundation can be reinforced, but in other cases it must be partially replaced or heavily upgraded. That structural scope drives cost and feasibility.

Key factors:
- Age, condition, and type of the foundation and framing
- Soil conditions and previous additions or modifications
- Current building codes and seismic requirements in your area
- Access for reinforcement work and temporary supports during construction

Before committing to a second story, budget for structural analysis and be open to plan B options (such as rear or side additions) if your existing structure cannot be cost-effectively upgraded. A reputable contractor will not promise a second story without verifying structural capacity first.
